Insects have evolved fascinating strategies to survive in the wild, especially in avoiding predators. Insects use colours to conceal themselves from their enemies. Combinations of red, black or yellow are used as warning colours. By using these colours, they warn their enemies not to hunt them. For example, ladybirds with their red and black colours send a message that they are terrible in taste. Similarly, the colours of the bees and wasps indicate that they can inflict painful stings. Some insects use both, colour and camouflage to ward off the predators. They camouflage themselves by looking like something else. The grasshoppers hide among plants and twigs as their colours look the same. The stick insects are very good at disguising themselves. With their long, slender bodies, they can hold themselves still and look exactly like the twigs they are resting on. Their eggs are also camouflaged to look like plant seeds. Such adaptations demonstrate how nature equips even the smallest creatures with tools for survival.

आज आवश्यकता है कि हम मौन की गरिमा को समझें, उसे जीवन में स्थान दें और महसूस करें कि सबसे गहरे संवाद कभी-कभी शब्दहीन होते हैं।
